The main takeaway from our work is that

we have cloned and characterized a novel C2-domain containing protein, which we named BAP3 (brain angiogenesis inhibitor 3), and which interacts with the cytosolic domain of BAI1 (BAI1 associated protein 3) and is predominantly expressed in brain.
BAP3 interacts with BAI-1, a protein that is a member of the p53 tumor suppressor gene family, in a manner that is not mediated by the BAP3 C2 domains.
BAP3 is the first C2 domain-containing BAI-interacting protein to be identified and that it may play an important role in the function of BAI1.
